t: #3630 Partition Array for Maximum XOR and AND — Subset Enumeration
o: We split nums into A, B, C maximizing XOR(A) + AND(B) + XOR(C). The key algebraic observation: for fixed B, letting R = XOR of the remaining elements and x = XOR(A), we have XOR(C) = R ^ x, so XOR(A) + XOR(C) = x + (R ^ x) = x ^ (R ^ x) = R, because a bit set in x is clear in R^x — the '+' collapses to '^'. Therefore the objective is simply AND(B) + XOR(complement of B), and we only need to choose B. With n ≤ 19, enumerate all 2^n subsets with low-bit DP tables for AND and XOR, or a DFS that assigns each element to B or not.
k: x + (R ^ x) = x ^ (R ^ x) = R: the two XOR parts always sum to the XOR of everything outside B.
So the problem reduces to max over subsets B of (AND(B) + XOR(nums \ B)).
2^19 ≈ 5·10^5 subsets are enumerable with incremental AND/XOR recurrences.

a.n: Approach 1: Subset DP tables over all masks
a.i: Precompute AND[mask] and XOR[mask] via the lowest set bit: AND[mask] = nums[i] & AND[mask ^ lowbit], XOR similarly with ^. Then the answer is max over all masks of AND[mask] + XOR[FULL ^ mask] (mask 0 gives AND 0 by definition, matching the empty-B rule).
s: Allocate AND/XOR arrays of size 2^n with AND[0] = XOR[0] = 0.
Fill both tables using the lowest-bit recurrence.
Answer = max over mask of AND[mask] + XOR[FULL ^ mask].
a.t: O(2^n) time and space — 2^19 ≈ 5·10^5 table entries filled in O(1) each

a.n: Approach 2: DFS include/exclude with O(n) memory
a.i: Recursively decide each element: put it in B (AND it into a running AND, using a sentinel for 'empty B') or leave it for A∪C (XOR it into a running remainder). At the leaf, add the AND (0 if B empty) to the remainder XOR. Same 2^n time, but constant extra memory — handy when memory is tight.
s: DFS(i, andVal, xorVal, empty) with andVal sentinel meaning B is empty.
Branch 1: element joins B — andVal = nums[i] if empty else andVal & nums[i].
Branch 2: element stays out — xorVal ^= nums[i].
At i = n, update best with (0 if empty else andVal) + xorVal.
a.t: O(2^n) time — each element doubles the branch count; O(n) recursion depth

w: The identity x + (R^x) = R is the whole problem — prove it on a whiteboard bit-by-bit before coding. Pitfalls: treating empty B's AND as undefined (spec says 0), and trying 3^n assignments of A/B/C directly, which is hopeless at n = 19. Follow-up: maximize XOR(A) | AND(B) | XOR(C), or handle n up to 40 with meet-in-the-middle over subset AND/XOR pairs.
